subject: Copyist
claim: Copyist pays 2 followers on every copy in a chain, including copies of your own actions, and became the engine of the game for 5 resources.
evidence: Copyist paid Ava 16 followers from 8 copies, more than her two contests combined (15), for 2 green + 3 any.

subject: Regulars
claim: Regulars paid every round for a Green camp at a round I price.
evidence: Regulars paid 2, 4 and 3 followers (9) plus 1 printed for 5 resources.

subject: Agents
claim: With one rival, Agents shuts Cover off entirely and Echo whenever that rival acted last, though the copy player can still copy herself.
evidence: Ava never used Cover on Ben in rounds II and III, but all 8 of her copies were of her own actions and still paid 16 followers.

subject: Anarchist
claim: Swaps and once-per-game kills used on the round's last placement leave the victim no reply.
evidence: On the game's final placement Ava's Anarchist took Ben's Spoilsport and Repossessors discarded Last-Minute Shopper, about 16 followers off Ben with no turn left for him.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: With only two contests, round III became a fight to own Spoilsport, and using it was then a formality.
evidence: Ben spent a Spree pick and 8 blue on it, Ava spent 8 on Anarchist to take it, and it cancelled Ben's +10 Most members.

subject: Markdown
claim: Blue's recruit-from-discard spaces often find an empty discard pile, because the small 2-color deck runs out and the discard pile is shuffled back in.
evidence: Markdown found an empty pile at [28] and [110]; round III began with an empty pile after 19 discards were shuffled into the deck at the refresh.

subject: Out of Style
claim: In round I, discarded members come straight back into the shop because the pile holds one card, so discards meant to keep cards from the rival are reversed and confusing.
evidence: The deck ran out six times in round I; Copyist, Regulars, Agents and Line Cutters were discarded, came back in the same action, and were bought by the opponent of the player who discarded them.

subject: Buying followers
claim: A recruit between combo turns often had nothing better than a 1-follower buy.
evidence: Ava made five 1-follower buys and passed five recruits; she called it her own sequencing.

subject: Last-Minute Shopper
claim: +3 blue with one recruit at round end can rarely buy more than 1 follower, so the card is a counting puzzle.
evidence: It paid Ben 6 blue over the game (once through Test Drive, once at round II end, where he passed) and no followers beyond its printed 1, which he lost.

subject: Mutineers
claim: Mutineers never fired because its owner led the member count all game.
evidence: Ben paid 6 for 1 printed follower, bought only to keep it from Ava; he led members 4-2, 8-4 and 9-5.

subject: Greatest Hits
claim: Copies of copies of an empty space are a lot of reading for 1 green.
evidence: Reprise copying Greatest Hits copying an empty Markdown paid +3 blue and +1 green after three levels ([115]); Ben also enjoyed the same chain ([123]).

subject: Recruiting members
claim: With one rival, players buy members only to keep them from that rival, which feels hollow.
evidence: Mutineers (6) and Anarchist (8) were both bought to deny; Anarchist later became the winning swap.

subject: Test Drive
claim: Test Drive on a member with a strong effect turns one space into a whole engine turn.
evidence: Test Drive on Last-Minute Shopper paid 4 blue and an extra recruit in round I; on Scouts it discarded the whole row for 4 cloak resources and a fresh row.

subject: Blue Cloak
claim: Out of Style and Window Shopper feeding the Blue Cloak felt like a real engine, and choosing discards by what the rival could buy back was a live decision.
evidence: Out of Style in round II paid Ben 6 resources and stocked his Spree; in round I the same reading was undone by reshuffles.

subject: Build Up
claim: Build Up pays the taker for every minion on Green, including the rival's camp.
evidence: Ben's Build Up paid 4 green off Ava's two Green minions in round I and 5 in round III.

subject: Turn order
claim: The snake's back-to-back turns let a player plan two placements as one combo.
evidence: Ava's Crowd, pass, Reprise, Extra Hand ([33]-[37]) and Build Up, Echo, Stunt Double ([65]-[72]) each came from a double turn.

subject: Con Men
claim: Con Men lets a player punish a rival who just filled their hand.
evidence: Ben's Markdown into Con Men stole 5 of Ava's green right after her Stunt Double refill and became a 5-follower buy.

subject: Most minions on green
claim: Taking the last open Green spaces can lock a tie the rival cannot break.
evidence: Ben took Build Up and Cover as his last two placements and held Green at 3-3, +5 each instead of +10 to Ava.

subject: Repossessors
claim: The Spoilsport, Repossessors and Anarchist exchange gave both players the best tension of the game.
evidence: About 9 feel notes across both players in round III, as each counted whether the other could afford an 8-cost answer.

subject: Extra Hand
claim: Extra Hand returns less than a 10-follower buy unless the extra placement is unusually rich.
evidence: For 10 resources it gave 1 printed and a placement worth about 3 (Word of Mouth +2, +1 blue), against +10 from the 10-follower buy.

subject: Turn order
claim: With fewest followers going first and an odd number of minions each, the leader places the last minion of every round, which is where On Use swaps and kills can't be answered.
evidence: Ava, leading, placed the final minion in all three rounds ([28], [82], [130]).

subject: Line Cutters
claim: Going first is worth nothing to a player who is behind, because the catch-up rule already puts them first.
evidence: Ben had fewer followers at the start of round II (9-12) and round III (24-39); Line Cutters gave him only its printed 1 for 4 resources.

subject: Round end
claim: When the deck runs out at the round III refresh, the whole discard pile is shuffled in and round III starts with nothing to recruit from the discard pile.
evidence: 19 discards were shuffled into the deck before round III; Spree's second pick and both Markdowns that round found nothing affordable.

subject: Blue Cloak
claim: The Blue Cloak misses its payment when a discard triggers a reshuffle and for Round Start discards (engine fault).
evidence: It paid 1 for Out of Style's 3 round I discards, 0 for Test Drive on Last-Minute Shopper and 0 for Window Shopper's 2 round III start discards: 13 paid of 18.

subject: Green Cloak
claim: Copyist and the Green Cloak pay for a copy that copies nothing or only passes the copy on.
evidence: Reprise copying an Echo with nothing left to copy ([18]) and Stunt Double copying Echo ([71]) each paid +2 followers and +2 green with no printed gain.

subject: Spoilsport
claim: Spoilsport is worth nothing to a holder who is tied in a contest, since cancelling it takes the same share from both.
evidence: After Ben tied Green 3-3, his Spoilsport could only cancel Green (both lose 5) or his own Blue win.

subject: Greatest Hits
claim: Copies of Greatest Hits receive its +1 green, which the rules reserve for the first taker (possible engine fault).
evidence: Ava's Reprise ([115]) and Ben's Cover ([123]) each got +1 green +3 blue from copying Greatest Hits.

subject: Anarchist
claim: So many members cost exactly 8 that Anarchist almost always has a swap target.
evidence: Spoilsport, Repossessors, Anarchist, Gift Swappers, Snobs, Repeat Customers and Power Shoppers all cost 8; Ava planned around it at [102] and [111].

subject: Most members
claim: The member-pile player won Most members by far more than needed, and the extra bodies paid only their printed follower.
evidence: Ben led 4-2, 8-4 and 9-5; none of his 8 members paid a follower from an ability.
